title: Pilot: tiered-token-bundle overflow credits + security-questionnaire invoice-hold flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers purchasing tiered token bundles are hitting overflow usage in high-variance months. Current behavior creates manual credits or retro invoice adjustments, leading to delays, disputes, and inconsistent accounting. Separately, enterprise security questionnaires occasionally surface compliance gaps mid-cycle; sales/legal ask for temporary invoice holds until remediation evidence is provided, but we lack an auditable, automated hold-and-release flow.

Goal: Run a two-arm pilot that (1) automates 'overflow credits' for tiered token bundles with configurable caps and ledgered journal entries that reconcile automatically on the next invoice, and (2) surfaces a security-questionnaire-triggered invoice-hold flow that places an operational hold at billing cutoff and auto-releases when checklist items are validated. The pilot must preserve accounting integrity, produce clear audit trails, and minimize manual ops.

Scope: Build metering + billing rules for token-bundle overflow calculation, ledger entry generation, UX for customer-facing invoice notes, customer success playbook, and a gated automation for invoice holds tied to a security-questionnaire status field in the contract record. Exclude refunds for chargebacks (separate flow).
acceptance_criteria: Overflow credits are computed automatically for customers on tiered token bundles according to config (percent cap, fixed cap, or shadow-charge) and a ledger entry is created in accounting that matches the invoice adjustment
Overflow automation runs without duplicate adjustments for 1000 simulated billing cycles (idempotency validated)
Invoice note and portal UI clearly show overflow credit, original charge, and net due; CS can view audit trail in Console
Security-questionnaire invoice hold can be toggled by Security/Legal via Console, creates an invoice hold flag, and prevents invoice finalization at cutoff
Auto-release logic releases holds when required checklist items are marked done and a signed remediation attestation is uploaded; release creates audit entry and triggers invoice generation
End-to-end metrics dashboard shows reduction in manual credits, mean time to resolution for holds, and number of disputed invoices during pilot
Accounting sign-off received and sample GL entries verified with ledger sandbox
comments: 2025-02-19 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff call with Billing, Legal, CS. Agreed pilot customers: 3 existing enterprise SMBs (opt-in). Action: Billing to prototype ledger entry format; Eng to estimate metering rule work.

2025-02-22 — Marco Ruiz: Engineering spike complete. Metering service can emit overflow events; two open questions: how to handle mixed-unit products (embeddings vs generation tokens) and whether overflow should be billed instantly or applied as credit. Recommend credit-on-next-invoice for accounting simplicity.

2025-02-25 — Priya Menon (Accounting): Reviewed ledger sample. Need 'original_charge', 'overflow_credit', and 'net' line items plus unique adjustment IDs. Also require idempotency token on adjustment API.

2025-03-01 — Legal (Ethan Zhou): Security-questionnaire hold acceptable; must include SLA clause for maximum hold duration (30 days) and notification taxonomy. Also request audit log retention of 7 years for enterprise customers.
2025-03-03 — UX (Leah Kim): Uploaded invoice mock with expandable credit details and hold banner. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/ux/invoice-overflow-hold-mock.png
2025-03-05 — Marco Ruiz: Branch created and PR opened for metering + billing rule logic. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/14892. QA scheduled for 2025-03-10.
notes: Experiment arms: A) Auto-create 'overflow_credit' ledger entries applied next invoice; B) Auto-bill overflow as immediate charge and email CS — pilot will run Arm A for lower ops impact.

Edge case: mid-cycle downgrade of reserved capacity should prorate bundle size and adjust overflow calculations; we will create a separate reconciliation job to run at downgrade time and surface proposed credits for manual approval during pilot.
Operational runbook: CS gets a queue item when a hold is placed; Legal/Customer to provide remediation evidence via secure upload. Internal Slack channel #billing-pilot for alerts.
Success metrics: <25% manual credit submissions for pilot customers, <5 disputed invoices/month, and <48h mean time to release holds.
Rollout plan: 2-week pilot with 3 customers, review at week 2, expand to 10 customers if metrics look good.
